title: What BIM is
sub: A building as a database with a 3D view
cards/0/body:
In BIM (Building Information Modeling) a building is assembled not from triangles but from objects: wall, door, window, slab. Each one has a type, a storey, materials, a fire rating, a manufacturer, a cost.

It is a database that happens to have a 3D view.
cards/1/body:
A mesh is a photo of a finished LEGO model: you see what it looks like.

BIM is the LEGO set itself, with instructions: every brick knows what it is, what it clips onto and how much it costs.
cards/2/task: Find the doors on the second floor, then tap “Save as GLB” and see what is left.
cards/3/q: What was left after saving as GLB?
cards/3/options/0: Only geometry: the properties and relationships are gone
cards/3/explain: GLB is a display format. It has no idea what a “door” or a “storey” is.
cards/4/q: What does a BIM door object know that a mesh does not? Select all.
cards/4/explain: A mesh knows the look too. But meaning, place in the building and properties belong to BIM alone.
cards/5/options/0: To compute quantities and cost, check codes, find clashes and hand data over to facility management
cards/5/explain: Schedules, cost estimates and timelines all come out of a BIM model. Geometry is only part of the data.
cards/6/body:
The architect, the structural engineer, the HVAC, plumbing and electrical engineers: each in their own program.

To bring it all together you need a common language, IFC, and a federated model for coordination.
